cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Only ~25% of organizations are scaling AI with a strategy, says Marketing AI Institute's Mike Kaput
stories.plain: Marketing AI Institute's Mike Kaput breaks down why most companies are stuck in pilot purgatory — running AI demos that never turn into real capability. With only about one in four organizations scaling AI strategically, this interview gives newcomers a clear lens for why governance and capability-building matter more than launching yet another proof-of-concept.

stories.head: The data trust crisis: Why your customer data is getting worse
stories.plain: A MarTech Conference session explains how data decay quietly destroys personalization ROI — outdated, inaccurate customer records feed bad signals into AI models, producing wrong recommendations and wasted spend. The piece outlines how to build a high-trust measurement framework, which is foundational before any CDP or AI decisioning layer can work reliably.

stories.head: Attentive VP: Lifecycle marketing is shifting from writing rules to setting direction for agentic AI
stories.plain: Attentive's VP of Strategic Accounts explains how agentic AI is taking over campaign decisions — choosing timing, channel, and message — while marketers shift from rule-writers to goal-setters. This reframes how customer engagement platforms are bought and staffed, and signals what skills teams will need as automation deepens.

stories.head: Why AI hasn't solved marketing's time problem
stories.plain: Faster content production from generative AI hasn't freed up time for strategy — instead it has created more content volume with no extra thinking time. This piece challenges the core ROI claim made in most AI-tool sales pitches and is essential reading for anyone evaluating whether a generative AI purchase will actually change how their team works.

stories.head: Growing restaurant chains beat rivals on local search and AI visibility, SOCi research finds
stories.plain: SOCi research shows a measurable gap: expanding chains dominate local search rankings, reviews, social signals, and AI answer visibility — while shrinking chains are invisible in generative engine results. This is one of the first studies to quantify GEO at scale for a single vertical, making it directly useful for multi-location marketers planning 2027 budgets.

stories.head: Rapid AI changes mean GEO is a weekly job now
stories.plain: AI-generated answers change fast enough that optimizing for them can't be a quarterly task anymore. PR, SEO, and content teams need a shared weekly process tracking what buyers ask, which sources AI cites, and what shifts. This reframes GEO from a one-time tactic into ongoing operational work — a new budget and workflow demand for marketing teams.

stories.head: The data trust crisis: Why your customer data is getting worse
stories.plain: Personalization and ROI both depend on clean customer data, but data decay is quietly undermining both. This piece from MarTech Conference coverage explains how to build a high-trust measurement framework — a foundational governance issue that affects every AI model or agent trained on first-party data.

stories.head: Marketing AI Institute's Mike Kaput: only ~25% of organizations are scaling AI with a strategy
stories.plain: Mike Kaput argues that most companies are stuck running demos that never become real capabilities. Only about one in four organizations has a repeatable scaling strategy for marketing AI. The distinction between a pilot and a capability is the single most important question buyers and practitioners face when committing budget and headcount to AI programs.

stories.head: Attentive VP: Agentic AI is shifting lifecycle marketing from rule-setting to direction-setting
stories.plain: Attentive's VP of Strategic Accounts explains how agentic AI is taking over campaign decisions that marketers used to encode as rules. Instead of configuring flows, teams now set goals and guardrails. This is a clear, practitioner-level description of how agentic decisioning is changing how CEPs are bought and operated.

stories.head: 10 Salesforce Winter '27 updates marketers need to know
stories.plain: Salesforce's Winter '27 release brings Agentforce-powered campaign creation and cleaner reporting directly into the platform most enterprise marketing teams already run. When a dominant CEP bakes agentic AI into core campaign workflows, it changes what buyers expect from every competing platform and raises the baseline for the whole category.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: The Data Trust Crisis Undermining AI-Driven Marketing
body: Marketers are discovering that AI systems are only as good as the data feeding them, and right now that data is degrading. Multiple reports this month confirm that marketers already know their AI tools are ingesting bad, outdated, or incomplete customer data — yet most have not fixed the pipelines supplying it.

The downstream effect is compounded: flawed data skews AI decisions, hidden costs inflate apparent ROI, and autonomous stacks can act on corrupt inputs before any human catches the error. Fixing data quality is now a prerequisite for AI credibility, not an afterthought.

themes.head: Governance & Autonomy Gaps in the AI Stack
body: Autonomous agents are being wired into marketing stacks faster than governance frameworks can catch up. A loophole identified this month shows that agentic systems can execute consequential actions with no human checkpoint, while a separate audit found most marketers are failing a basic AI governance test they do not even know exists.

The pattern is clear: tools like Docusign's Agreement Layer and Focal AI's agentic wealth platform signal that agents will soon sign, spend, and commit on behalf of brands. Without clear accountability structures, the liability lands on marketers who never reviewed the policy.

themes.head: GEO Is Now a Weekly Discipline, Not a Campaign
body: Generative Engine Optimization has crossed a threshold: AI search surfaces change their ranking logic so frequently that monthly or quarterly GEO reviews are already obsolete. Brands that treat visibility in AI-generated answers as a set-and-forget task are ceding ground to competitors who treat it as an ongoing editorial process.

OpenAI's claim about ad revenue and SOCi's case study on local restaurant chains both reinforce the same point — being findable inside AI-generated responses is becoming a primary acquisition channel, and the rules governing it shift faster than traditional SEO ever did.

themes.head: AI Pilots vs. Scaled Capability: Only 25% Cross the Line
body: Marketing AI Institute's Mike Kaput crystallised a divide that explains much of the hype-vs-reality gap: roughly 75% of organisations are still running isolated AI experiments rather than building repeatable, organisation-wide capabilities. A pilot produces a demo; a capability changes how decisions get made at scale.

This structural gap is why AI hasn't solved marketing's time problem despite years of investment. Speed gains stay local — trapped inside one team's workflow — rather than compounding across the organisation. Closing the gap requires strategy, not more tools.

themes.head: The Agentic Infrastructure Layer Is Being Built Now
body: Across CRM, CX, identity, and video, this month's product launches share one architectural bet: the next competitive moat is infrastructure that lets AI agents act, not just advise. Salesforce Winter '27, Alchemer's Iris, Focal AI, and Fimo's self-improving websites all embed agent-readiness as a core feature rather than a bolt-on.

Identity and trust are emerging as the chokepoints. Socure & NextgenID's high-assurance IAL3 partnership signals that agentic systems will need verified identity rails before enterprises trust them with real transactions. Marketers who understand this infrastructure layer now will have procurement leverage when it becomes table stakes in 2027.

month.takeaway: The month's noise resolves into one structural truth: AI in marketing has moved from experimentation to infrastructure, and the organisations that treat data quality, governance, and agentic readiness as strategic bets — not IT tickets — will set the terms everyone else follows by 2027.
